sanskrit: ud ehi devi kanya ācitā vasunā saha | na tvā taranty oṣadhayo bāhyāḥ parvatīyā uta ||
english: Rise up, O goddess, O maiden, laden with wealth! The herbs that are of the plains and those of the mountains do not surpass you.

sanskrit: yathā tvā devy oṣadhe sarvaḥ kāmayate janaḥ | evā bhagasya no dhehi devebhya ivāmṛtaṃ pari ||
english: As every person desires you, O divine herb, so bestow upon us the bounty of Bhaga, even as the immortal draught is poured about for the gods.

sanskrit: utsaktapatny oṣadha āvataṃkaraṇīd asi | yad eṣi yan niṣīdasi tatra tvāhaṃ sam agrabham aśvam ivāśvābhidhānyā ||
english: O herb, you are the one who loosens the bonds of the womb — you are the maker of earrings. Wherever you move, wherever you settle, there I have seized you, as a horse-tether captures a horse.

sanskrit: yathā kumāras taruṇo mātaraṃ pratinandati | evāsmān prati nandatu yāṃ vayaṃ kāmayāmahe ||
english: As a young boy rejoices to greet his mother, so let the woman whom we desire rejoice in greeting us.

sanskrit: trīṇi pātrāṇi prathamāny āsan tāni satyam uta bhūtaṃ tatakṣa | ṛtasya māne adhi yā dhruvāṇy ebhir devā amṛtaṃ bhakṣayanti ||
english: Three vessels were the first to exist; truth and existence fashioned them. Upon the measure of ṛta rest those that are immovable — with these do the gods partake of the immortal draught.

sanskrit: svar yad devā vibhajanta āyan trīṇi pātrāṇi prathamāny āsan | ādityā ekaṃ vasavo dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ rudrā adhi saṃ babhūvuḥ ||
english: When the gods came distributing the heavenly light, three vessels were the first to exist: one the Ādityās claimed, the Vasus a second, and the Rudrās took possession of the third.

sanskrit: dhātā veda savitaitāni sarvā bṛhaspatiḥ prathamo devo agniḥ | ebhir indro jaṭharam āpṛṇīte tribhiḥ pātrair uta viśve ca devāḥ ||
english: Dhātṛ knows all these; Savitṛ knows them; Bṛhaspati, the foremost god, and Agni. With these three vessels Indra fills his belly, and likewise all the Viśve Devāḥ.

sanskrit: ūrdhvā tiṣṭhanti na nu jihmā bhavanti nonaṃ babhūva katamac canaiṣām | devānāṃ pātrāṇi nihitāni yāni tāni saṃ pāti ya ṛtasya gopaḥ ||
english: They stand upright; they do not become crooked; not one among them has become diminished. The vessels of the gods that have been set in place — he who is the guardian of ṛta watches over them all.

sanskrit: paurṇamāsī prathamā yajñiyāsīd ahnāṃ rātrīṇām atiśarvareṣu | ye tvāṃ yajñair yajñiye bodhayanty amī te nākaṃ sukṛtaḥ paretāḥ ||
english: The full-moon night was the first among those worthy of sacrifice, surpassing the days and nights in the watches of deep darkness. Those who awaken you, O night worthy of worship, with sacrifices — those, the well-doers who have passed on, reach your vault of heaven.

sanskrit: pūrṇā paścād uta pūrṇā purastāt paurṇamāsī madhyata uj jigāya | tasyāṃ devaiḥ saṃvasanto mahitvā nākasya pṛṣṭhe sam iṣā madema ||
english: Full behind and full before, the Paurṇamāsī has risen supreme in the middle. Dwelling together with the gods in her greatness, may we rejoice on the ridge of the vault of heaven with refreshments.

sanskrit: catasro diśaḥ pradiśo ha pañca ṣaḍ urvīr āhū rajaso vimānīḥ | dvādaśa rtava ārtavāś ca te mā- -ā pyāyayantu bhuvanasya gopāḥ ||
english: The four quarters and indeed five intermediate directions, the six broad spaces they call the measurers of the atmosphere — the twelve seasons and those that belong to the seasons: may they, the guardians of the universe, cause me to swell with fullness.

sanskrit: yathādityā aṃśum āpyāyayanti yam akṣitam akṣitayaḥ pibanti | evā mām indro varuṇo bṛhaspatir ā pyāyayantu bhuvanasya gopāḥ ||
english: As the Ādityās cause the soma-stalk to swell, which the inexhaustible ones drink inexhaustibly, so may Indra, Varuṇa, and Bṛhaspati, the guardians of the universe, cause me to swell with fullness.
